title: YNX Creator Studio — Content, rights, teams, and revenue evidence
metaDescription: A Web-first YNX Testnet creator console for team access, content workflows, rights review, analytics evidence, revenue records, and bounded AI proposals.
h1: Create with explicit rights, roles, and evidence
directAnswer: YNX Creator Studio is the professional control console for creator teams. Its local candidate manages content, rights, analytics, revenue evidence, moderation, and human-reviewed AI proposals while Wallet, Pay, Trust, and Data Fabric remain separate authorities.
features: Channel-owned team roles with immediate persisted revocation
Source-hash-bound rights declarations and independent review
Fail-closed media processing and publication boundaries
Human-reviewed AI proposals that cannot publish or move assets
risks: The current candidate is locally tested but not centrally integrated or publicly deployed.
Local Testnet revenue and analytics records are not proof of real-world value, audience, availability, or profitability.
Central Wallet, Pay, Trust, Data Fabric, monitoring, security, and release acceptance remain required.
Production signing, immutable hosted downloads, store release, and public runtime evidence are absent.

faq.question: Can a team member redirect creator payouts?
faq.answer: No. Team and AI roles cannot sign, withdraw, or redirect creator assets; payout intent remains owner-controlled and requires canonical Wallet and Pay acceptance.

faq.question: Can the creator verify their own commercial rights?
faq.answer: No. Commercial eligibility requires an independent rights review whose declaration remains bound to the uploaded source SHA-256.

faq.question: Can AI publish content automatically?
faq.answer: No. AI output is a proposal that requires explicit human review and cannot publish, assert rights, move funds, or change team authority.

faq.question: Is Creator Studio publicly released?
faq.answer: No. The repository contains a locally tested Web candidate. Central integration, staging, public deployment, hosted artifacts, production signing, and store release are not evidenced.
